chief_complaint: chronic diarrhea, severe weight loss, and oral thrush
hpi_details: 35M presents with a 2-month history of non-bloody watery diarrhea, extreme fatigue, and a 20-pound weight loss. He also complains that his mouth hurts and he has thick white patches on his tongue and inner cheeks.
ideas: thinks he has a bad stomach bug
concerns: terrified about his rapid weight loss
expectations: wants a cure for his diarrhea
social_hx: History of IV drug use, multiple sexual partners

core_concepts: Oral candidiasis (thrush) in a young, otherwise healthy adult without recent antibiotics is a major red flag for severe immunosuppression (HIV).
Chronic diarrhea and wasting are AIDS-defining conditions.
common_misconceptions: Treating the thrush without investigating the underlying cause of immunosuppression.
dangerous_errors: Failing to offer HIV testing in patients presenting with opportunistic infections.
management_principles: HIV screening (4th gen Ag/Ab test), CD4 count, viral load, treat opportunistic infections, initiate ART when appropriate.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 35M with chronic diarrhea, significant weight loss, and painful white oral plaques.
reference_soap.objective: Cachectic. Oropharynx shows thick white removable plaques on erythematous bases (Candidiasis).
reference_soap.assessment: Suspected advanced HIV infection (AIDS) with oral candidiasis and HIV enteropathy/wasting.
reference_soap.plan: Offer and perform HIV 1/2 Ag/Ab screening. Start oral Fluconazole for thrush. Order stool studies for opportunistic pathogens (Cryptosporidium, MAC). Infectious disease consult.

learning_objectives: Recognize oral thrush in an adult as a potential indicator of HIV infection.

teaching.one_liner: Young adult with severe weight loss, chronic diarrhea, and oral candidiasis highly suspicious for advanced HIV.

must_ask.say: How long have you had the diarrhea, and is there any blood in it?
How much weight have you lost, and over what period of time?
Have you noticed white patches in your mouth, or pain when swallowing?
Have you ever been tested for HIV, and do you have any risk factors like unprotected sex or IV drug use?
Have you had a cough, shortness of breath, or vision changes?
